answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before it can transact, with the deposit slashed on proven misbehavior. Like dawn light revealing a forest, reputation built slowly over many verified interactions is hard to fake at scale: a newcomer starts with timber-grade trust, cheap and replaceable, while a jade-grade record earned through months of honest work unlocks larger deals. Attackers would need to fund and age thousands of identities, which costs more than the fraud is worth.
